extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, scientists, advocates, and community groups who want to participate in federal rulemaking
extracted.subtask_short: writing public comments for federal rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing science-informed written and oral public comments to federal agencies during the rulemaking, permitting, and enforcement processes; includes recommendations for equitable participation and testimony at hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite peer-reviewed studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under UCS's Key Comment Quality Criteria as a central element of science-informed comments; reflects the organization's emphasis that laws and regulations should be better backed by science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish consensus science from emerging research
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between consensus science and emerging research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UCS recommends explicitly noting whether evidence represents broad scientific consensus or newer, less-established findings so agencies can weigh certainty appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge uncertainty ranges
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend documenting the degree of uncertainty in scientific findings (ranges, confidence limits, limits of inference) when presenting evidence to the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique the agency's scientific evidence base where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique the agency's scientific evidence base where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UCS advises reviewers to evaluate and, when warranted, point out gaps, weaknesses, or outdated elements in the agency's scientific support for the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest specific scientific updates the rule should incorporate
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggest specific scientific updates the rule should incorporate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond critique, commenters should propose concrete scientific changes or additions that agencies can adopt to strengthen the rule's evidence base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify environmental justice and equity dimensions of the science
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify environmental justice/equity dimensions of the science
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UCS recommends calling out how scientific findings affect different communities and highlighting equity concerns so agencies consider distributional impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write effective written comments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a Key Focus Area; UCS provides guidance (via its resources) on structuring and composing written comments so they are clear, persuasive, and usable by agency staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare structured oral testimony for hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Testifying at public hearings (structured approach to oral public comments)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UCS offers a guide titled 'How to Testify at a Government Hearing' that advocates using a structured approach when delivering oral comments to the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand permitting and enforcement decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UCS's 'A Citizen's Guide to the Federal Regulatory Process' includes material on permitting and enforcement to help commenters target their input appropriately within those processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure meaningful participation and fair access for frontline communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring frontline communities can participate meaningfully; Fair Access: Guidance for Meaningful Public Participation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UCS emphasizes recommendations for equitable access and practices that enable frontline and marginalized communities to participate effectively in rulemaking and other decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use science to inform participation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core principle: UCS believes submitting public comments backed by scientific evidence improves laws and regulations; commenters are encouraged to ground arguments in science where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit comments to the official record
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting a public comment to the record is an important way to make your voice heard in the policymaking process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UCS frames comment submission itself as a key participatory act that contributes to agency decision-making and accountability.
